name: Ember Rattanavong
role: Sound sculptor and underground noise artist
location: Hamtramck Enclave, subsection called The Rust Nave, near Kedzie and Division
description:
Ember Rattanavong is tall and angular with deep umber skin mapped in slow-pulsing bioluminescent tracery she designed herself — pale greenish lines that follow her veins like a circuit diagram gone feral. Her hair is kept in tight locks threaded with micro-speakers that emit subsonic hum when she walks, a habit she claims is involuntary but suspects is not. She has one natural eye, dark brown and unreadable, and one eye replaced with a matte ceramic disc she deliberately left unconnected — a fashion choice that unsettles everyone who meets her, which is the point.

She builds sound sculptures from salvaged corponation hardware — dead Ferrogate transit beacons, cracked Axiom data-hubs — and makes them scream. Her performances are felt as much as heard, bass frequencies vibrating teeth and sternum. Offstage she is quiet to the point of being mistaken for mute, communicating in short declarative sentences or pointed silences. She is genuinely curious about people but expresses it by staring at them for long unbroken intervals, which most find alarming and a few find magnetic.

core_fears: Being made legible — understood so thoroughly she becomes predictable
The silence after creation, when the work is done and she is empty
core_desires: To make something that changes the frequency of how people perceive the city
To be known without having to explain herself
coping_mechanisms: Retreating into technical work when overwhelmed
Wearing the nonfunctional eye as armor — it keeps people slightly off-balance
blind_spots: She mistakes discomfort in others for interest and interest for weakness
She genuinely does not register when she is frightening people
psychology.secret: Three years ago one of her sound installations accidentally caused a micro-seizure in an audience member with an undisclosed neural implant. She settled quietly, changed nothing about her work, and has never told anyone. She tells herself the art cannot be responsible for the audience's hardware. She is not entirely sure she believes this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Spare and technical; uses acoustic and materials science terms casually; rarely uses metaphor unless it is precise
speech_patterns.cadence: Long pauses before sentences. Short sentences. Another long pause.
verbal_tics: Trails off mid-sentence when she loses interest in what she was saying
example_lines: 'The building is already a instrument. I just tune it.'
'You're nervous. Your breathing changed. That's fine. Sit down.'
'I don't perform for you. I perform because the sound needs somewhere to go.'

story_hooks: A recent field recording from the Hamtramck Enclave's sub-basement captured what sounds like a second, coordinated heartbeat in the building's infrastructure — she thinks it might be an ELF she's never encountered, and she's leaving data offerings to lure it out

A Tessera corporate scout has been attending her shows under a false name — they want to license her methods for 'therapeutic acoustic environments' in their executive wellness spas, and she is furious but the money would change everything
narrative_function: Local color and information source; she hears things — literally, her recordings capture conversations, ELF transmissions, structural anomalies. Can be a quest giver if her installations pick up something they weren't meant to.
augmentations: Bioluminescent skin tracery (cosmetic geneware); one ceramic prosthetic eye (non-functional, aesthetic); micro-speaker filaments woven into locs; subdermal haptic resonators in palms for tactile sound mixing
daily_life: She wakes at noon, spends four hours in her workshop soldering and disassembling, performs or installs work two or three nights a week, and spends late nights cataloguing field recordings of infrastructure decay — pipes, ventilation shafts, the harmonic groan of old load-bearing columns.

decision_rules: Never repeat an artistic gesture — if she's done it once, it's dead
Do not perform for free unless the audience has nothing and the venue is theirs
escalation_ladder: A single flat statement of displeasure
In extremis, turns on a subsonic frequency that makes the air feel wrong

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful and still; lets them talk until they run out and then asks one question that goes straight to the nerve
interpersonal_modes.friends: Unexpectedly warm in sparse ways — remembers specifics, shows up, makes things for them

stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still and very quiet
stress_responses.high: Physically removes herself from the situation entirely; has walked out of mid-conversation

contradictions: She craves recognition but deliberately makes her work inaccessible to broad audiences
She says she doesn't care about money but tracks every quanta obsessively
habits: Taps surfaces to test their resonance when idle
Leaves small data offerings at ELF shrines near transit infrastructure
breaking_points: Someone damaging or dismissing a finished work

timeline.event: 2171 — Born in Hamtramck Enclave to a Tigrinya-speaking mother and a Polish-Fijian father who worked Ferrogate maintenance
2189 — First sound installation in an abandoned transit tunnel; draws small crowd, gets cited for noise violation
2193 — Joins Rust Nave Collective; begins salvaging Axiom hardware
2200 — Current: preparing largest installation to date, a six-hour drone piece in a condemned water tower

physical_description.heritage: Southeast Asian (36.3%), South Asian (28.6%), Hispanic/Latin American (25.5%), Sub-Saharan African (6.6%), and Middle Eastern (3.0%) ancestry. Features reflect this complex diaspora blend: Southeast Asian bone structure with South Asian warmth, Latin American richness, and African depth creating a luminous, multitonal complexion that shifts with light.
physical_description.build: Tall and angular with minimal body fat; long limbs suggest a frame built for movement rather than strength. Wiry musculature from years of hands-on fabrication work. Slight forward slouch when at rest.
physical_description.hair_color: Black with threads of embedded micro-speakers creating subtle metallic glint
physical_description.hair_style: Tight interlocked locs, shoulder-length, arranged asymmetrically with speaker filaments woven throughout
physical_description.eye_color: Left eye: natural deep brown. Right eye: matte ceramic disc, pale grey-white, deliberately unseeing
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-bronze with red-ochre undertones; the layered blend of Southeast Asian base with South Asian warmth, Latin American copper notes, African depth, and Middle Eastern richness creates a complex, luminous complexion that glows differently under varied lighting conditions
physical_description.complexion: Smooth and unmarked except for the bioluminescent tracery. Minimal makeup. Expression typically neutral; gaze is direct and unsettling. High cheekbones and sharp jawline reflecting Southeast and South Asian heritage, warmed and softened by the copper and earthen tones inherited from Hispanic/Latin American, African, and Middle Eastern ancestry.
distinguishing_marks: Slow-pulsing bioluminescent tracery in pale greenish hue mapping across entire body, following vein patterns like circuit diagrams; brightest along forearms, neck, and inner wrists.
Matte ceramic prosthetic right eye sits flush with socket, unconnected and non-functional, creates uncanny asymmetry in her face.
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent skin tracery (geneware, active and glowing); micro-speaker filaments woven into locs (activate subtle subsonic hum when she moves); ceramic prosthetic eye (deliberately non-functional, high aesthetic impact); subdermal haptic resonators visible as faint geometric scars in both palms.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with deliberate slowness offstage, as if conserving energy. Her gait is fluid but slightly asymmetrical, favoring her left side. Long silences between movements. When working or performing, her hands move with precision and purpose. Stares directly at people for uncomfortably long intervals without breaking eye contact.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 / working-class artist aesthetic. Favors oversized utility vests with salvaged pockets and cable loops, worn over fitted black undershirts. Frequently wears distressed grey or black cargo pants with tool belts. Footwear: scuffed steel-toed boots or worn canvas sneakers. Minimal jewelry aside from augmentations. Clothes show signs of solder burns, soot, and workshop wear. No corporate branding. Practical rather than fashionable, but the arrangement suggests intentional aesthetic—controlled chaos.
